page.layout: Top: running head with page number, two circular portrait medallions with captions (left and right). Below them: one column of text in two paragraphs (ACURSIUS, DINUS). At the bottom: a decorative woodcut ornament with no text.

main_text.p: ACURSIUS natione Florentinus, juris consultissimus, fuit. Azonis Doctoris discipulum fuisse eü perhibetur, qui cum admirabili ingenio, & multarū rerum cognitione, valeret, Reipublicae moderandae maximè idoneus, universum juris Civilis corpus, primus glosis ornauit & explanauit. Huius autem libros semper imprimendos curauere docti, ubicunque fuit excusum corpus Juris, cum glosis & commentariis: eáque de causa omnium Jurisconsultorum celeberrimus existimatur, utpote qui primus Jus Civile interpretatus fuerit. Floruit is anno salutis 1236. ut ipse in Autetica testatur. Scripsit etiam super instituta.

DINUS Mugelanus Juris utriusque peritissimus, tāta fuit animi solertia, ut omnes suę ætatis Jurisconsultos superasse creditus sit. Fuit acutus & eloquens in dicendo, disputando & decidendo: & idcirco eleganter & copiosè totum jus Civile, multis scriptis, expofuit & clarius legum studiosis reddidit. De mādato Bonifacij Papę viii. primus eleganter, post Archidiaconū, scripsit super 6. Decretalium lib. 1. super Codice lib. 10. super ff. veteri libr. 24. super ff. nouo. libros 12. super ff. Infortiato lib. 14. Consilia multa lib.1. super Titulū de actionibus in Institutis. Super titulū, De regulis Juris, & infinita alia quę nō reperiuntur. Floruit anno salutis 1300.

page.notes: Two circular woodcut portraits sit above the text; their captions are transcribed as lines. Bottom ornament is a woodcut with no printed text. Medallion captions were read from the scan; the letters of "ACCURSIUS" and "MAGELL." are at the edge of the circle and may be partly worn. The running head and page number are at the top, not in the margins. No catchword or signature is visible.
